summary: Investigated the silent timestamp issue under concurrent redirects and verified the fix by making last_accessed_at monotonic with an atomic GREATEST upsert.
evidence: Reproduced one concurrent burst (10 requests to the same short link) and compared request timestamps against analytics.last_accessed_at.
Before change, timestamp drift evidence showed last_accessed_at could lag the latest observed request completion timestamp under concurrency.
Applied atomic upsert change in api/app/main.py: last_accessed_at = GREATEST(analytics.last_accessed_at, EXCLUDED.last_accessed_at) while preserving count = analytics.count + 1.
Post-change burst comparison showed no timestamp regression behavior and count correctness remained intact (all requests returned 307 and count increments were preserved).
Residual difference between analytics.last_accessed_at and latest HTTP completion time is expected because last_accessed_at captures database write-time semantics, not response completion time.
